newsitem.title: UK: Bass confident of continued H2 progress.
newsitem.headline: Bass confident of continued H2 progress.

text.p: Bass Plc, the UK brewing and leisure group, said on Wednesday it was confident of continued progress in the second half of the year in a trading statement covering the first 48 weeks of its financial year.
Chairman Sir Ian Prosser said: "We are confident that overall we will continue to see good progress in the second half of the year even after allowing for the exceptional summer last year."

In a divisional breakdown, it said that hotels had seen dollar-based profits growth in the second half, but at a slower rate than the first half. To date revenue per available room in U.S. franchised hotels rose six percent.
In Europe, the Middle East and Africa revenue per available room was up eight percent.
In leisure retailing, Bass Taverns saw turnover growth of 16 percent. Drinks takings per outlet fell seven percent, but food revenues were up 60 percent.
Bass Leisure saw operating profits fall below last year. The National Lottery has hit some of the betting businesses.
Bass Brewers saw a strong performance, with beer volumes up 2.5 percent on 1995.

In the Britvic soft drinks unit, the Robinsons brands sold well and profits were in line with forecasts, but tough competition and "cool summer weather" was blamed for reduced profits on the Britvic brands.
